blogs.title: Young Adult, Old Cells: When Pancytopenia Plus Fibrosis Should Trigger a Telomere Biology Workup
blogs.description: This post would use the case to highlight a high-yield pattern recognition problem: a young adult with unexplained cytopenias, premature greying, liver disease and interstitial lung abnormalities. It would discuss when clinicians should move beyond isolated organ-based thinking and suspect a telomere biology disorder, even in the absence of the classic dyskeratosis congenita mucocutaneous triad.

blogs.title: B12 Deficiency Was Real—But Not the Whole Story: Avoiding Premature Closure in Ineffective Erythropoiesis
blogs.description: This post would focus on the diagnostic tension created by severe vitamin B12 and folate deficiency. It would examine how megaloblastic features, low reticulocyte count and marrow erythroid hyperplasia can explain pancytopenia, yet still coexist with a deeper inherited marrow vulnerability. The teaching point is how to recognize when a confirmed nutritional diagnosis is insufficient to unify the full syndrome.

blogs.title: The DAT Trap: Interpreting a Positive Coombs Test in the Context of Marrow Failure and Intramedullary Hemolysis
blogs.description: This post would explore the common bedside dilemma of a positive direct antiglobulin test in a patient with anemia and biochemical evidence suggestive of hemolysis. Using this case, it would review why elevated LDH, indirect hyperbilirubinemia and DAT positivity do not automatically equal autoimmune hemolytic anemia, especially when the reticulocyte response is low and the marrow picture supports ineffective erythropoiesis.

blogs.title: Cryptogenic Cirrhosis and Early Pulmonary Fibrosis: The Liver-Lung Axis of Telomere Disease
blogs.description: This post would center on the extra-hematologic manifestations of telomere biology disorders, especially hepatic fibrosis/cirrhosis and pulmonary fibrosis in younger patients. It would discuss how these findings are often investigated separately, delaying recognition of a unifying inherited syndrome, and would review the growing relevance of telomere disorders in so-called idiopathic fibrotic disease.

blogs.title: A VUS with a Phenotype: How to Use Clinical-Genetic Correlation Without Overcalling the Variant
blogs.description: This post would tackle the practical genomics lesson in the case: a monoallelic PARN missense variant classified as a variant of uncertain significance, but strongly supported by phenotype and gene-disease biology. It would cover how clinicians should interpret VUS results, integrate ACMG-style evidence cautiously, avoid false certainty, and still use the result to guide surveillance, counseling and subspecialty follow-up.

blogs.title: What Changes After the Diagnosis? Management Pearls in Adult Telomere Biology Disorders
blogs.description: This post would focus on downstream management once a telomere biology disorder is suspected or identified. Topics would include serial monitoring for marrow failure, pulmonary and hepatic progression, malignancy risk, family counseling, transplant considerations, and why recognizing these syndromes early matters even when immediate treatment remains largely supportive.
